title: Faecal adrenal and thyroid hormones as markers of cold stress in Florida manatees (Trichechus manatus latirostris)
content:
Abstract
Florida manatees (Trichechus manatus latirostris) are susceptible to cold stress syndrome (CSS), a chronic, sometimes lethal, multisystem disease associated with skin lesions, emaciation, dehydration and secondary infections. To investigate endocrine changes associated with CSS, we compared faecal adrenal (cortisol and aldosterone) and thyroid hormone [total triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4)] metabolite concentrations among manatees that died due to CSS, presumed healthy manatees that died acutely from watercraft collision injuries and live, apparently healthy wild manatees. Faecal T3 showed the strongest and most consistent association with health status, with CSS manatees exhibiting concentrations approximately three times higher than healthy animals. Elevated T3 concentrations may reflect increased thyroid hormone activity associated with thermoregulatory demands, nutritional stress or both. Faecal T4 was also elevated in CSS manatees, though this result was sensitive to the exclusion of calves and is complicated by strong cross-reactivity of the T4 assay with reverse T3 (rT3). Faecal cortisol concentrations were more strongly associated with size class than health status, with calves showing higher concentrations than adults regardless of group, potentially reflecting developmental and life-history factors including weaning and hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis maturation. Faecal aldosterone showed an overall marginal effect of health status that was not maintained in pairwise comparisons or sensitivity analyses. Faecal hormone concentrations in manatees that died from acute watercraft injuries did not differ significantly from those of live, apparently healthy animals, providing some support for the interpretation that the differences in CSS manatees reflect ante-mortem physiological state rather than post-mortem sampling effects. Multivariate hormone profiles differed among health groups in the full dataset, though these patterns were strongly influenced by the disproportionate representation of immature animals in the CSS group. Together, these findings identify faecal T3 as a promising non-invasive indicator of CSS and improve understanding of endocrine responses to cold stress in manatees.
